memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system, a dispatch[]-reachable agent's contract file can serve as the routing target for BOTH the research and implement phase of the same routing entry (10 such dual-role agents exist across the present and filetypes extensions, e.g. budget-agent, grant-agent, filetypes-router-agent). When authoring a per-agent obligation block meant to vary by phase (e.g. a status-enum sentence that differs between research/plan/implement), check whether the target agent is dual-role via the manifest's routing_agents.research/.implement values before assuming a single variant applies — a dual-role file needs a combined variant that conditions its phase-specific sentences on which dispatch it is currently serving, not one of the three single-phase variants.

For a mechanical, near-identical markdown insertion across many agent contract files that share a common template (Stage N headings under '## Execution Flow', followed by a top-level '## Error Handling' or '## Critical Requirements' section), a robust generic insertion anchor is: find the LAST heading matching '^#{2,3} Stage \d+' in the file, then find the next '^## ' heading after it, and insert immediately before that next heading. This anchor is level-agnostic (works whether the last Stage heading is ### or, inconsistently, ##, as seen in grant-agent.md) and reliably lands the new subsection as a sibling of the final Stage heading, before the next top-level section -- avoids needing per-file manual placement across dozens of files with otherwise-uniform structure.
